question: Does native transport improve completed deterministic document work or its cost over the same signed path-vector application over numeric TCP/HTTP?

design.baseline: Existing numeric TCP/plain HTTP harness with the same signed path-vector routing, encryption and durable receipts; no TLS. Not libp2p, conventional A2A or all IP deployments.

CI_operator.identity: Temporary in-memory key of our isolated PR CI; not an independently verified operator

conclusions: Neither scenario crosses the predeclared 20% paired median p95/wire screening threshold. Practical superiority is not established.
Both transports correctly completed all 800 tasks, including 200 exact duplicate replays, without duplicate execution.

In the relay-outage scenario, paired median native/TCP ratios are 1.385759 for total work duration, 1.127195 for captured work-phase bytes and 8.014071 for recovery. These are descriptive ratios from one host, not statistical or WAN claims.

Median absolute recovery was 2618174 us native and 326484 us TCP/HTTP. The first post-fault request in pair 0 records one native TimeoutError (2617038 us) versus three TCP ConnectionRefusedError retries (322069 us). This is consistent with the existing 2.5-second native hop timeout and TCP fail-fast behavior; a new controlled ablation is needed for causal attribution.
p95 alone hides the single outage stall. Keep completion time and recovery alongside per-request latency. Median paired ratios are not ratios of unpaired medians.
checks: All six app PR checks green: verify, audit, container-pilot, native-ethernet, reproduction-reference, practical-comparison

20 full observations and pcaps independently reverified locally against the pinned CI public key; paired metrics, receipts/hops and frame counts recomputed
53 frozen files, 26 strict commits, five signed historical bundles and prior 147 canonical history events preserved

104 research/history/auth/A2A tests passed in the existing complete interop environment; three new projection tests reject tamper, wrong key and wrong domain; 96 pages and 2393 editorial strings in each of three translations checked
negative_results: First local suite found the old exact-nine experiment count; the new track makes ten. Scoped loopback permission resolved the other sandbox-only local failures.
Both comparison scenarios miss the preregistered benefit threshold; native outage completion and wire costs are worse. No threshold, retry, timeout or result was altered after observing the data.
The first research test environment lacked httpx/PyYAML and the sandbox denied local sockets; the existing complete interop environment and scoped loopback execution passed all 104 tests.
remaining_questions: Preregister a separate fixed-timeout/fail-fast ablation before changing native recovery behavior; retain this original comparison as the control.
Repeat on a dedicated runner and independent hosts/operators, with transport security parity and a power/uncertainty plan before broader performance claims.
Real LLM answer quality, paid model cost, WAN behavior, human setup effort, governance and business value remain unmeasured.
operational_limits: No merge, production deployment, production Actions, live-server experiment, model invocation, foreign code, operator admission or resource allocation
Signatures authenticate statements and packet bindings, not operator independence, external time or the truth of plaintext answers; the committed runner checks deterministic answers at runtime
The public projection checks signed scope and paired summaries. Full receipt/hop/capture reanalysis also needs the retained complete artifact; its raw pcaps are not in this public projection
Five pairs per scenario on one CI host, fixed virtual topology, static neighbor admission, sequential paced tasks and trusted reference code; not a hostile-code sandbox

Native has signed link framing; the TCP/plain HTTP baseline has no TLS. CPU excludes the parent capture process; peak RSS is a sum of per-process peaks. EtherType absence by itself is not practical benefit
